comparison: Use square-integrable real functions under the stated measure on the bounded domain, then quotient by almost-everywhere equality to obtain the definite L2 norm and Hilbert-space interpretation. MemLp.toLp explicitly constructs that equivalence class; the literal set of measurable functions has only a seminorm because distinct representatives may differ on null sets. The source does not state the quotient or all underlying measure-space conventions, so record this as a required interpretation rather than silently rewriting its definition. eLpNorm represents the higher-p expression in extended nonnegative reals and retains possible infinity. Membership in L2 on a bounded domain does not imply finite Lp norm for p>2; even finite-measure embeddings apply in the opposite direction. Do not use conversion of infinity to real zero to claim a finite norm, and pointwise evaluation of later random functions requires representative conventions separately.
